doc.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025

title: Streaming, royalties and distribution
summary: His view that streaming pays creators almost nothing, and that he leaves business matters to others and uses a digital distributor.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you have an opinion about the way music is delivered to listeners now?

Sure. I mean it’s, you know it’s horrendous how much creative — how little creative people are paid for streaming. It’s virtually nothing. And it’s, you know it’s a terrible problem but this has been a terrible problem for years that we used to sell physical units of stuff and now we don’t. And trying to persuade people to buy some physical product is really difficult when you can pretty much hear everything streaming somewhere. So you know I mean the problem is much bigger than you and me and I have no — I don’t have any solutions.
Well to be specific, why are the songs from “Hallucination Box” readily available on YouTube? Did you do that?

No. I didn’t do that. But I do get Internet royalties which have been going up a little bit, as modest as they are. So I can’t speak very intelligently about any business issues. I’m not good at it. I think I have a fair knack for putting one note next to another note, and I’m still doing that. That’s about as far as it goes. I defer to wiser heads when it comes to the business stuff. I don’t understand it all that well. I do have a digital distributor that makes sure that those albums are available on Apple Music and what used to be iTunes and so forth.
